doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Hartwick and the CBS staff years
title: Tape two: length of the studio years and the end of staff orchestras
summary: Jones was in network studio work nearly twenty years until the staffs were discontinued and the shows moved to California.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It is Saturday, November 27, 2004. My name is William A Brauer Junior. I am at the home of Henry William Jones Junior conducting an interview for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Project. The engineer is Sven Abu. This is tape number two. I've read 17 years, and 20 years. But, what is the length of time that you were first in the studio, TV, radio, recording world?

It was less than 20 years because I wanted to join the 20-year club. You had to work there for 20 years to be like Specs Powell. It was just short of 20 years. It was something along the lines of 17 or maybe 19.
The whole thing just shut down. CBS… Well, actually ABC, NBC – – they all shut down at the same time. All the shows moved to California at about that time…
All the shows with the staff orchestras.

Right. Well, they discontinued the staffs. The point they made was that staffs were not needed anymore because there was not enough work coming in to justify the use of staff. The demographics showed that, for instance, on that Ed Sullivan show, it showed that the people who watched the Ed Sullivan show were not the
people who bought the products that the sponsors sponsored. That is why the show went off the air.
